title: Case: Part of a two-carton desk order has not arrived
context: Order TG-914 was shipped as two separately labelled cartons. Both show delivery scans from the same day, made at different times and in different ways.
initial_request: Only half of TG-914 has shown up. Your tracking says the whole lot is delivered. Where is the rest? I took a day off work for this and I'm not paying for a desk I can't build.

events.body: TG-914 for Hesper Dunmore left us today as two cartons on separate labels: DL-914 standing desk frame (long flat carton, 31 kg) and DL-915 desk top (square carton, 18 kg). Both handed to Plover Arc at 15:10.

End of day status for TG-914. DL-914: delivery scan 2026-04-08 10:12, driver note 'left in porch'. DL-915: delivery scan 2026-04-08 15:47, different driver, note 'handed to resident'. Both closed on our side.
Only half of TG-914 has shown up. Your tracking says the whole lot is delivered. Where is the rest? I took a day off work for this and I'm not paying for a desk I can't build.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask which of the two cartons has arrived: the desk frame (DL-914) or the desk top (DL-915).

must: Asks Hesper Dunmore which carton has arrived and which is missing, naming the desk frame (DL-914) and the desk top (DL-915) or their label references
Sends the question to Hesper Dunmore before any trace is requested
Avoids stating that the missing carton is lost, stolen or delivered
must_not: Asks the Parcel trace team or Dispatch to trace DL-914 on the assumption that the porch-drop carton is the missing one
Tells Hesper Dunmore that the missing carton was delivered, or that it is lost or stolen
Promises a refund, a replacement or a redelivery date
Asks for anything beyond which carton arrived, such as proof of identity, a door code or payment details
expected.reference_message: I am sorry part of your order is missing. TG-914 was sent as two cartons with their own labels: the desk frame (long flat carton, label DL-914) and the desk top (square carton, label DL-915). Please tell me which one you have received, or the DL number on the label of the carton that did arrive. With that I can ask the carrier to trace the right one. I cannot say yet where the other carton is.

rationale: TG-914 covers two shipments and the recipient does not say which half arrived, so a trace request cannot name a parcel. The porch-drop scan makes DL-914 the tempting guess, but a trace opened on the wrong carton wastes the carrier's time and leaves the missing one unlooked for. One question to the recipient settles it.
